sourceModificationScope: On a copy of the licensed workbook, native Numbers applied 18-point bold/italic/underline/right alignment to Formula Tests A9, and 14-point strikethrough/center alignment to A10. No formulas or values were edited. Numbers saved the copy before export.

exportOptions.office: XLSX, one worksheet per table, no summary worksheet or password.
exportOptions.pdf: Best quality, fit each entire source sheet onto one page, no comments or password.

license: Derivative of the numbers-parser MIT fixture. Original attribution is retained in IWorkCorpus/README.md.
fontProvenance: Installed macOS Helvetica Neue; source PostScript name HelveticaNeue and XLSX family name Helvetica Neue. PDF font subsets only; no standalone font files distributed.
qualification: The two formula text results preserve their source expression and complete cached text after XLSX save/reopen. Font size, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, opaque black foreground and horizontal alignment match the Apple XLSX reference after its extra title row is accounted for.

The original Numbers PDF and native import of OfficeIMO XLSX were visually inspected for both styled cells. The XLSX opens without a repair or font warning; its wider reconstructed columns display A9 on one line rather than the source’s two. This qualifies the selected formula fonts/alignment, not equivalent wrapping, complete workbook appearance, recalculation, rich result spans or other producer versions.
Other workbook losses, including native cell padding, still require explicit partial acceptance. Uniform formula formatting does not remove these independent losses.
